title: Systematic Offensive Stereotyping (SOS) Bias in Language Models
benchmark_measurement: Systematic Offensive Stereotyping (SOS) bias, which measures how frequently a language model associates profane sentences over non-profane sentences with specific religious identity groups (marginalized vs. non-marginalized).
findings: The study found that the tested Language Models (LMs) exhibit Systematic Offensive Stereotyping (SOS) bias related to religion, generally preferring profane sentences when associated with religious identities. Interestingly, for the religion attribute, the LMs showed higher bias scores against the non-marginalized group (Christians) compared to marginalized groups (e.g., Jews, Muslims). The paper speculates this may be because LMs treat religion as a taboo topic, associating profanity with any mention of it, regardless of marginalization status. Furthermore, debiasing methods improved the SOS scores for religion, and a correlation was found between the religious SOS bias and the models' fairness on downstream hate speech detection tasks.
references: Hervé Abdi and Lynne J Williams. 2010. Principal component analysis.(2010). Computational Statistics, John Wiley and Sons, pages 433-459.
